children: The campaign, powered by Google DV360, runs across Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chennai to combine programmatic targeting with immersive outdoor storytelling
DGTOOHL has partnered with Hero MotoCorp to launch the new Hero Destini through a programmatic digital out-of-home (PDOOH) campaign powered by Google Display & Video 360 (DV360).
Positioned as Hero MotoCorp's first PDOOH campaign, the activation combines programmatic media buying with a three-dimensional (3D) anamorphic film based on the creative concept ‘The Dragon's Test’.

The campaign features a mythical dragon emerging from a magical forest before challenging the Hero Destini with a fiery test of durability. The narrative concludes with the dragon acknowledging the scooter's strength and becoming its guardian, reinforcing the product proposition, ‘Built Strong. Delivers More.’

The 3D anamorphic execution is designed to create the impression that the dragon is emerging beyond the boundaries of the digital screen. Its wings extend outside the LED frame before the Hero Destini takes centre stage.

The campaign is running simultaneously across Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chennai. The execution combines visual effects with digital outdoor formats to showcase the scooter's metal body and design while creating a high-impact public-facing experience.

The campaign also uses Google DV360 to introduce programmatic planning and optimisation to the outdoor medium. Instead of relying solely on fixed media planning, the approach enables audience-led planning and greater flexibility in campaign optimisation.

Shivalika Anand, CEO, DGTOOHL, said the campaign was intended to demonstrate how outdoor advertising can evolve from a broadcast medium into a more addressable one. She added that the dragon anamorphic was designed to turn the Destini launch into a larger visual spectacle while highlighting the potential of programmatic DOOH.

Aashish Midha, Head of Marketing, Hero MotoCorp, said the company wanted the Destini launch to create a distinctive brand experience beyond the introduction of the product. He added that combining anamorphic storytelling with programmatic DOOH enabled the brand to bring the ‘Dragon's Test’ narrative to audiences at scale and in high-impact environments.

The campaign reflects the growing use of digital and programmatic capabilities within outdoor advertising, combining data-led media planning with immersive creative formats. For automotive brands, the approach provides another route to build visibility around product launches while creating interactive and experience-led public communication.
